events.why: This tests weekend access for families and day-workers who are turned away when the library is closed, while shortening two weekdays to keep staffing close to the current budget.

events.reason: The schedule change is supported as a thing to test, and the simulation already shows many turnaways when the library is closed. The staffing/budget claim is not supported by any local source, so it should be treated as an unsupported real-world input.
ungrounded: Shortening Wednesday and Friday to 09:00-15:00 will keep staffing close to the current budget.

events.summary: Tue/Thu/Sun access: 4.1 ± 1.3 vs 0.0 ± 0.0 for current practice (visits/week by residents who can't make current hours). E5 has the highest measured benefit for the target metric: 4.1 ± 1.3 visits/week for residents who can’t make current hours, versus 0.0 ± 0.0 under current practice. It also beats E1/OS at 2.9 ± 1.2, E4 at 2.7 ± 1.0, and SW at 3.9 ± 1.1, while holding performance up in held-out tests (E5: 3.125, 7.125, 7.875 vs E1/OS: 1.875, 4.125, 5.625).
events.assumptions: The comparison depends on synthetic resident schedules, arrival rates, and word-of-mouth rates; staff-hour estimates are also taken as given (E5: 93 h/wk vs current practice: 75 h/wk).
events.pilot: Run a 6-8 week pilot with Tue/Thu 09:00-19:00 and Sun 12:00-16:00, then measure weekly visits by residents who cannot make current hours, total visits, and staff hours used; compare against the pre-pilot baseline of 0.0 ± 0.0 visits/week.
